issues.legal_issue: An institution meeting the statutory definition of a math is a public religious endowment subject to the Act, even if public access to its premises is disputed.
material_facts: The institution was presided over by a Mahant who exercised spiritual headship over disciples and preached to them.
Succession to the Mahant’s office was regulated by the institution’s usage.
The institution had disciples, provided religious services, and its properties supported activities connected with the institution and religious devotees.
The appellant disputed that the institution was public and claimed that the public had no right of entry or worship.
issues.conclusion: The institution was a math as defined in the Act and was a public math; its premises and administration were subject to the Act as a Hindu public religious endowment.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(a), 6(7), and 6(12), including the explanation to section 6(12), an institution is a math if it promotes the Hindu religion, is presided over by a person engaged in spiritual service or exercising spiritual headship over disciples, and succession to that office follows the founder’s directions or usage. A math’s premises are included in a religious endowment, including where they are used for both religious and secular purposes. The Court held that a math within the statutory definition is a Hindu public religious endowment. The beneficiaries of a math include its religious fraternity and people of the relevant faith, who constitute at least a section of the public; the Court left open whether a private math can exist.

rule.if: institutional_status_dispute and promotes_hindu_religion and spiritual_headship_over_disciples and succession_regulated_by_founder_or_usage

predicates.institutional_status_dispute: A dispute concerns whether an institution qualifies as a math and is subject to religious-endowment regulation.
predicates.promotes_hindu_religion: The institution exists to promote the Hindu religion.
predicates.spiritual_headship_over_disciples: A person presiding over the institution engages in spiritual service or exercises spiritual headship over disciples.
predicates.succession_regulated_by_founder_or_usage: Succession to the presiding office follows the founder’s directions or the institution’s usage.

issues.definition: When an institution is disputed as to its status and it promotes the Hindu religion, has a spiritual head over disciples, and succession to that office is governed by directions or usage, it is treated as a public religious endowment subject to regulation.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff who sues to set aside an administrative determination classifying an institution and its properties as religious-endowment subject matter bears the initial burden of showing that the determination is wrong.
material_facts: The Commissioner determined that the institution was a math as defined in the Act and that the properties were religious endowments.
The plaintiff brought suit under the statutory procedure to set aside that determination and obtain a declaration that the Act did not apply.
The Commissioner’s determination was final subject to the result of the suit.
issues.conclusion: The initial onus was on the plaintiff to establish prima facie that the institution was not a math as defined and that the properties were not endowed properties.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 64(1) and (2), the Commissioner decides whether an institution is a math or temple, and an affected person may sue to modify or set aside that decision; the decision remains final subject to the suit’s outcome. Unlike the situation discussed in Parma Nand v. Nihal Chand, the plaintiff here sought to displace an existing administrative determination, so the initial burden rested on the plaintiff.

predicates.suit_challenges_administrative_classific: A plaintiff brings a suit seeking to set aside an administrative decision classifying an institution or its property.
predicates.prior_determination_remains_effective_su: The administrative decision remains effective unless and until the suit changes it.

issues.definition: If a suit challenges an administrative classification that remains effective subject to the suit, the challenger bears the initial burden of showing it is wrong.

issues.legal_issue: A gazetteer may be consulted as historical material on matters of public history and institutional practice, but not as evidence of title.
material_facts: The High Court relied on a gazetteer’s account of religious institutions, their practices, and the institution in dispute.
The gazetteer was relied on for historical information and practice, not to establish title to property.
issues.conclusion: The gazetteer could be consulted on matters of public history; the Court treated its statements as historical material and evidence of practice, not as evidence of title.
issues.legal_principle: A gazetteer may be consulted on matters of public history. Its historical descriptions and accounts of practice do not thereby become evidence of title.

predicates.gazetteer_consulted_for_public_history: A court consults a gazetteer for historical information or accounts of institutional practice relevant to public history.
predicates.not_relied_on_to_establish_title: The gazetteer is not relied on to establish ownership or title to property.

issues.definition: A gazetteer used for public history and not to establish title may be consulted as historical material.

issues.legal_issue: Property acquired or held in a Mahant’s name may be found to belong to the math where the evidence shows institutional use and the claimant does not establish personal acquisition or ownership.
material_facts: The properties were claimed by the appellant as personal or private properties, but documents concerning acquisitions were generally in the names of the Mahants.
A gift deed referred to the benefit of disciples and their successors in perpetuity and concerned land forming part of the math site.
Other documents connected property with religious services, offerings, food distribution, or assignment to the math.
The Mahants were ascetics and heads of the institution; the evidence did not show that the disputed purchases were made from their personal assets.

The plaintiff did not produce all relevant documents, acquisition-funding accounts, expenditure accounts, or the consolidated budget, and evidence showed that private and math accounts had been mingled.
The record included a grant directing property income toward religious offerings and distribution of food among visiting Vaishnavas.
issues.conclusion: The disputed properties were properties of the math rather than the personal properties of the Mahant; the evidence did not support the appellant’s claims that the properties were personal or private.
issues.legal_principle: The name in which property is acquired does not by itself establish that it was acquired for the Mahant’s personal use; an acquisition for the math may be equally or more probable where the Mahant acted as its head and representative. The Court relied on Sitaram Days Banasi v. H.R.E. Board Madras and Raghbir Lala v. Mohammad Said for the significance of an acquirer’s status as an ascetic and institutional head. The purpose and use shown by the documents, the absence of evidence tracing acquisitions to personal assets, and the failure to produce relevant accounts and documents supported treating the properties as math properties.

rule.if: property_ownership_dispute and property_acquired_or_held_in_institutional_head_name and evidence_shows_institutional_use and not claimant_shows_personal_funding_or_use

predicates.property_ownership_dispute: A dispute concerns whether property belongs personally to an institutional head or to the institution.
predicates.property_acquired_or_held_in_institution: The property was acquired or held in the name of the person who headed the institution.
predicates.evidence_shows_institutional_use: Documents or other evidence connect the property or its proceeds with the institution’s religious, charitable, or operational purposes.
predicates.claimant_shows_personal_funding_or_use: The claimant establishes that the property was acquired from personal assets or was held for personal use.

issues.definition: Where ownership is disputed, property in an institutional head’s name is treated as belonging to the institution when the evidence connects it with institutional purposes and the claimant does not establish personal funding or use.
